title: Papa Celestin's 1941 band and its members
summary: Jiles played with Celestin for a few months in 1941 until Celestin was hurt, and names the sidemen.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money

blocks.x: Did you ever work with Papa Celestan?

Oh yeah, Celestan. I worked with him in 41 he made up a band. And at that time he had quit playing for a while, almost like give it up. And he started to make up a band. So I was playing with him and for then when the war come up you had to get a defense job. And he got a job now at the shipyard at Higgins. And some guy got loose with a car and run over to a gang of people and he was one of the guys that got hit. And we had played together, had a band of about two or three months, and after he got hit and crippled, well that dissolved. And then he got hit and then he got hit and then he got hit and then he got hit and then he got hit.
Who did he have in those times when you were with him?
Which one is that? That always confuses me.
Eddie Johnson and Edward Johnson. Is that where the confusion comes from? I don't know.
They got so many of them. What does he play?

Eddie Johnson the saxophone player. Is that the one that works for World Lines? Big Head Eddie. That's right, yeah. He had Eddie Johnson. He had Kit Clayton playing trumpet, Albert Walters. He had octave on piano. He had Ricard playing bass. And Trombo played Miss Valenta. He had the band. You mean Bill Matthews? Bill Matthews playing Trombo. Well, yeah. The Reeds? Do they have any Reeds?
I was trying to think of them. You must have had more than one. That's what I'm trying to think of. He had three. He had the. He had the. He had the John. Sam Lee on tenor. You know what I mean?
Yeah. I don't know about that.
I don't know about that. I don't know about that. I'm going to Gilbert's name.
Yeah, that's right. I'm talking to my hand. I asked him. Speaking about that clarinet, with the large rattles. Mm-hmm.
